steps.title: Prepare Coral Fragments
steps.instruction: Remove coral fragments from the freezer (if applicable) and soak them in individual 500 ml plastic beakers filled with deionized water for 30 minutes at room temperature to remove excess salt.

steps.title: Bleach and Clean Skeletons
steps.instruction: Remove organic tissue from the coral skeletons using sodium hypochlorite bleach and sonication.

substeps.instruction: Transfer coral fragments using plastic forceps to new 500 ml beakers containing ~200 ml of 3% sodium hypochlorite bleach.
Soak for 1 hour at room temperature, ensuring the fragile corallite micro-skeleton is not damaged.
Replace the bleach with fresh solution and sonicate in a sonicator bath for approximately 30 minutes at room temperature.
Visually inspect skeletons; if tissue remains (light brown or green), sonicate in fresh bleach for an additional 30 minutes or longer until completely white.

steps.title: Dry Skeletons
steps.instruction: Dry the cleaned coral skeletons in an oven.

substeps.instruction: Drain and dispose of the bleach.
Transfer skeletons into individual pre-labeled aluminum weighing pans.
Dry overnight at 60 °C in a drying oven.

steps.title: Capture Photomicrographs
steps.instruction: Use a Leica DMS1000 Microscope to take multiple images of each individual coral skeleton at various angles and magnifications.

substeps.instruction: Take low-magnification images to visualize gross morphology.
Take medium-magnification images from a dorsal view to visualize individual corallites.
Take multiple high-magnification images to visualize sub-corallite structures.
Adjust the skeleton angle between high-magnification shots to ensure corallites are photographed perfectly perpendicular to the field-of-view.

steps.title: Set ImageJ Scale
steps.instruction: Open a high-magnification photomicrograph in ImageJ and calibrate the scale.

substeps.instruction: Zoom into the upper left corner where the scale bar is located.
Use the 'Straight' tool to select the entire 1 mm scale bar.
Navigate to 'Analyze' > 'Set Scale', enter '1' in the 'Known Distance' field, and 'mm' in the 'Unit of length' field.

steps.title: Select Target Corallite
steps.instruction: Identify a suitable corallite for measurement within the software.

substeps.instruction: Zoom out and select a corallite that is perpendicular to the field-of-view (avoid tilted corallites).
Zoom in until the single selected corallite fills the entire ImageJ window.
Identify the dorsal directive septa and the clockwise arrangement: lateral pair 1, lateral pair 2, ventral triplet, lateral pair 3, and lateral pair 4.

steps.title: Map Septal and Thecal Points
steps.instruction: Use the 'Multi-point' tool to place specific coordinate points on the corallite structure.

substeps.instruction: Place points #1–#24: For each of the 12 septa (clockwise from dorsal directive), place one point at the outer end and one at the inner end. Use negative space (black holes) and the fossa ring as guides for consistency.
Place points #25–#48: Place two points on either side of each septa at the midpoint (halfway between the endpoints), proceeding clockwise.
Place points #49–#60: Place one point on the inner edge of the theca walls of neighboring corallites, opposite from the septa outer-edge points, proceeding clockwise.
Place point #61 at the center of the primary corallite.
Place points #62 and upwards in the center of all neighboring corallites that share a thecal wall with the primary corallite (typically 4–8 corallites).

steps.title: Export and Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Extract the coordinates and calculate skeletal measurements.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to 'Analyze' > 'Measure' (or Ctrl + M) to generate a Results window with X and Y coordinates for all points.
Copy and paste the coordinates into an Excel spreadsheet.
Calculate distances between points (e.g., septa length, width, theca thickness, corallite spacing) using the distance formula: $\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}$.
Calculate areas (e.g., Corallite Area or Fossa Area) using the coordinate polygon area equation.
